body: Quick pass (M5): the box check stays first; a flagged fixture is re-judged by its closed mesh against the carried stock's dexel columns (the new sim `FixtureMesh::steel_on_line`, reusing the BVH and parity rule) with 0.01 mm contact tolerance. The mesh can only CLEAR a box hit, never add one: an open or coarse mesh, an unreadable line, a spent budget or a sub-cell footprint keeps the box verdict. Time is bounded (column skip, 50 M facet-visit budget; worst case 0.39 s release). Seven app pins (vise held and moved in; nest clear, too small, near-miss 0.02 past and within tolerance) plus six sim tests; mutations red, including both tolerance directions. The quick gate, 23 app suites, sim fixture_mesh and clippy app/sim are green. #1530 is P2; collision check, so the safety tier. Flagged ready; a review by the other session is next.

Rework for the M3 review (pullrequestreview-5898561678). New head: 87f657fa (c4d127d2 fix, 87f657fa tests). It merges cleanly with upstream main.

**Rule chosen (blocker 1): read the material between the columns as whole rectangles, not lines.** Every rectangle spanned by four neighbouring material columns, trimmed by the 0.01 mm tolerance, is judged against the material the four share (highest floor to lowest top) by `FixtureMesh::steel_in_prism`. Why it cannot miss steel:
1. If a facet clipped to the rectangle reaches into the material slab, that facet has a point inside the slab, so the fixture is refused.
2. If no facet lies over the rectangle, there is no steel there: any steel point's vertical line leaves the solid through a facet at the same XY.
3. Otherwise the slab holds no surface. It is either all steel or all air, and one line through it decides.

Nothing inside the material is sampled, so the post and the lip are refused (3.00 / 4.00 mm). I did not take the per-cell envelope against the column's own material, or the box fallback wherever mesh features lie off the lines. Both refuse every gripping jaw whose face is not on a grid line, because the cell holding the part's edge reaches past it. Where the four columns disagree (a side face or a step), only what they share is judged. This is the box law's one-pitch resolution at a face. It is pinned, and stated in the decision record.

**Blocker 2.** A line whose winding goes negative, or does not close at zero, reads `None`, so the box stands.

**Blocker 3.** The app-level pins are listed in the body.

**Nudge.** It is capped at 0.1 micron a step (0.56 micron at most). Pinned with a 6 micron block at X 5000.

**Performance, re-measured in release.** With the budget, the 400 k-facet worst case stops at 0.34 s with the box verdict. Without a limit it takes 16.6 / 19.4 s.

Gate: all the requested suites are green, and clippy `-D warnings` is clean for app (all targets) and for the sim lib and touched test. Counts are in the body.

Ready for a re-review.
